strings.name: Arianna Huffington
strings.role: Writer, HuffPost co-founder and Thrive Global founder
strings.summary: Huffington moved from books and political commentary into digital media, co-founding The Huffington Post before building workplace wellbeing and behavior change services through Thrive Global. Her career spans online news and health entrepreneurship. Her early biographies also drew plagiarism allegations, which she denied; the Callas biography dispute ended in an out-of-court settlement.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded The Huffington Post, advanced online news models and developed workplace wellbeing services.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied economics at Girton College, Cambridge, and served as president of the Cambridge Union.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Helped build an online news platform
strings.highlights.h1.text: Co-founded The Huffington Post in 2005, bringing reporting, aggregation, blogs and reader discussion together. After AOL acquired the site in 2011, she continued in media leadership.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Moved from media into wellbeing
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded Thrive Global in 2016 around sleep, stress and daily habits, later expanding into an AI health coach project and a collaboration with Labcorp.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Launched a health testing collaboration
strings.timeline.t1.text: Thrive Global and Labcorp introduced the Thrive 5 Health Test, pairing health measurements with educational material on habits. Huffington described the collaboration as founder and CEO.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Helped establish Thrive AI Health
strings.timeline.t2.text: Thrive Global and the OpenAI Startup Fund announced a new company to develop a personalized AI health coach, aiming to make support for daily behavior change more accessible.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Left HuffPost and founded Thrive
strings.timeline.t3.text: Stepped down as The Huffington Post's editor-in-chief to focus on Thrive Global, turning themes of sleep, burnout and work from her writing into business services.
strings.timeline.t4.title: AOL acquired The Huffington Post
strings.timeline.t4.text: Following the acquisition, she became president and editor-in-chief of the AOL Huffington Post Media Group, extending her remit to other content brands in the group.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-founded The Huffington Post
strings.timeline.t5.text: Launched the news and blogging site with partners, helping shape commercial models for American online political commentary, news aggregation and community discussion.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entered and withdrew from California's recall election
strings.timeline.t6.text: Ran as an independent candidate in California's gubernatorial recall election, then withdrew before voting and opposed the recall of Governor Gray Davis.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Published a biography of Callas
strings.timeline.t7.text: Published Maria Callas. The book later prompted a plagiarism dispute with Gerald Fitzgerald that ended in an out-of-court settlement; she denied the plagiarism allegations.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entered public debate with her first book
strings.timeline.t8.text: Published The Female Woman, engaging in contemporary debates on women's liberation and social roles, before continuing into biography, politics and lifestyle writing.
